abstract: Predicting gene fitness under varying light environments remains a major challenge in photosynthetic organisms. During environmental shifts, the massive protein investment required for photosynthesis and photoprotection severely compresses the available enzymatic capacity for other core pathways, exhausting cellular metabolic redundancy. Standard flux balance analysis (FBA) relies on a single biomass-optimal solution and fails to capture this shrinking metabolic flexibility, particularly under CRISPRi-mediated partial repression. To address this, we developed FluxStack, a computational framework that transforms static metabolic networks into dynamic, enzyme-constrained flux landscapes. For the CRISPRi fitness task under different light conditions, we further introduced light-aware knockdown flux balance analysis (light-aware kdFBA). This method represents graded gene repression by reducing the catalytic capacities of reactions associated with the target gene and applying separate constraints for low and high light, rather than disabling these reactions completely. By integrating these spatial flux variations into multi view representations, FluxStack outperformed standard FBA in predicting binary knockout essentiality without relying on simple growth ratios. For the four-class CRISPRi task, strict nested five-fold cross-validation yielded an accuracy of 0.966 and a macro-F1 score of 0.960. These results suggest that integrating enzyme-capacity constraints with flux landscape sampling provides a powerful predictive lens for uncovering condition-dependent metabolic vulnerabilities in photoautotrophs.
